problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}-4\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+5y=20{e}^{4x}.
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Second-Order Inhomogeneous ODEs With Exponential Forcing

feedback.problem:
Given that the differential equation 

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}-9\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+18y=8{e}^{2x}
$$

has the complementary function ${y}_{c}(x)=A{e}^{3x}+B{e}^{6x}$, find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ to this equation.
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the complementary function is ${y}_{c}(x)=A{e}^{3x}+B{e}^{6x},$ the roots of the auxiliary equation are $\lambda =3$ and $\lambda =6.$

The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is $8{e}^{2x}.$ In this case, the constant factor in the exponent is $2$, which is not the root of the auxiliary equation. Therefore, we assume a particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}=\alpha {e}^{2x},
$$

where $\alpha $ is a constant that is to be determined.

Calculating the first and second derivatives of ${y}_{p}$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x}=2\alpha {e}^{2x},\,\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}=4\alpha {e}^{2x}.
$$

We substitute ${y}_{p},$ ${y}_{p}^{′},$ and ${y}_{p}^{″}$ into the ODE and solve for $\alpha :$

$$
\begin{aligned}4\alpha {e}^{2x}-9(2\alpha {e}^{2x})+18(\alpha {e}^{2x}) & =8{e}^{2x} \\ (4-18+18)\alpha {e}^{2x} & =8{e}^{2x} \\ 4\alpha {e}^{2x} & =8{e}^{2x} \\ \alpha  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=2{e}^{2x}.
$$
